metadata.title: Awesome Tactile Hands
metadata.scope: Public datasets that record touch across the hand during manipulation: human tactile gloves and dexterous robot hands with tactile sensing.

datasets.name: TouchScale
datasets.title: TouchScale: 500 Hours of Human Vision and Touch for Visual-Tactile Learning
datasets.summary: Bimanual tactile gloves with 880 taxels per hand, recorded with head-mounted RGB-D and two wrist cameras across about 2K everyday tasks.

sensor.note: Normal pressure, 1.5 x 1.5 mm cells, 15 pads over five fingers and palm (palmar side), spatial resolution below 2 mm. Hardware spec 50 Hz WiFi / 100 Hz USB; released data is 35-90 Hz, timestamped per sample. Release NPZ also carries tangential (shear) components per pad.

scale.text: 500 h, ~87K episodes, ~2K tasks, 1.5K+ objects, ~20 participants, 9 collection settings (800+ scene configurations)

datasets.access: Gated on Hugging Face. 100 h / 15,324 episodes / 929 tasks (~1.08 TB) released so far; the rest is planned before November 2026.
caveats: No hand-pose capture; the paper estimates pose with WiLoR.

cameras.resolution: 1280x720 RGB; depth 640x480 native (released registered to RGB at 1280x720)

tracking.note: Paper runs WiLoR on auto-detected hand crops for its experiments; no pose file in the release file list and no hand-tracking hardware.

unconfirmed: Glove maker not named; paper calls it the 'Tachin Glove' (product name only). Data were captured by vendor Noitom for Overfit Lab.
Transduction principle not stated (paper: 'flexible tactile sensing gloves', normal pressure).
scenes=9 is the paper's 'high-level collection settings' for the full 500 h; the 100 h HF release lists 22 finer scene types. scene_types are the 7 environments the paper names (of 9).
subjects: paper says ~20; the 100 h release card says 24 pseudonymous participants.
Release status: 100 h / 15,324 episodes / 929 tasks / 905+ objects on HF; 500 h planned before Nov 2026.
Paper says the glove records normal pressure only, but the release NPZ includes tf_tactile_x/y 'tangential components'.
Depth resolution: paper 640x480; card says depth_head.mkv is 1280x720 registered to head RGB.

datasets.name: EgoTouch
datasets.title: TouchAnything: A Dataset and Framework for Bimanual Tactile Estimation from Egocentric Video
datasets.summary: Bimanual pressure gloves with Rokoko finger tracking and Vive wrist trackers, a chest camera and two fisheye wrist cameras, 208 tasks in 5 kinds of scenes.
datasets.hand: Custom pressure gloves + Rokoko mocap gloves

sensor.note: 256 raw channels per hand; the release code maps 138 (left) / 147 (right) of them, of which 15 / 24 are finger bend sensors, leaving about 123 pressure taxels per hand. Remapped to a hand-shaped 21 x 21 grid; the glove also streams an IMU quaternion.

scale.text: ~20 h, 1,891 episodes, 208 tasks, 1,000+ objects, ~2.1M frames, 5 scene types

datasets.access: Hugging Face, 88.5 GB.
caveats: The paper reports 256 channels per glove; part of them are bend sensors, so the pressure taxel count (about 123) is derived from the release code.
Release counts differ from the paper: 1,933 episodes / 213 tasks on Hugging Face against 1,891 / 208 in the paper.

tracking.note: 21 joints per hand, transformed into the Vive frame via the wrist tracker when calibrated (rokoko_hands.json).
Three trackers (chest, left_wrist, right_wrist) via OpenXR; 7-D poses in vive_poses.json.
Release also ships wilor_hands.json (1,930 episodes) and hamer_hands.json (1,536 episodes).

other: finger bend sensors in the glove stream

sources: local: ~/data/ext/egotouch (episode files, split.json; ffprobe of chest/left/right.mp4)
unconfirmed: Camera models not stated. Egocentric camera is called head-mounted in the main text but 'chest/head-mounted' in the appendix; files are chest.mp4 and the Vive role is 'chest'. README calls it a 'wide-angle' camera.

taxels_per_hand=256 is the raw channel count. The released mapping (pressure_position_mapping_*.json) uses 138 (L) / 147 (R) unique channels; configs/hand_joint_positions.json marks 15 (L) / 24 (R) of them as finger bend sensors, leaving ~123 (L) / ~129 (R) pressure channels.
Glove maker not named ('custom pressure-sensing gloves'); raw file is named jq_pressure.json, which suggests but does not establish a JQ Industries glove.
Release counts differ from the paper: HF lists 1,933 episode folders / 213 tasks; local split.json lists 2,228 episodes / 228 tasks; paper and README say 1,891 / 208.
Number of participants not stated.
scenes/scene_types from the paper's five environment categories, confirmed by the release's top-level folders (Home/Office/Outdoor/Retail/Workbench).
taxels per hand (123) derived from the release's channel mapping, not stated in the paper

datasets.name: TactiDex
datasets.title: TactiDex: A Real-World Tactile-Guided Benchmark for Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Piezoresistive glove over a MANUS mocap glove with OptiTrack object tracking, single-hand and bimanual, retargeted to Inspire hands.
datasets.hand: Piezoresistive glove over MANUS Metagloves Pro

sensor.note: 162 elements per glove on fingertips and palm, worn over a MANUS mocap glove; force resolution up to 0.01 N.

scale.text: 757 sequences, 49 objects, 10 subjects, 5.1M frames, single mocap workspace

datasets.access: No data or code link on the project page or arXiv as of 2026-10-15.
caveats: No RGB video: pose comes from the MANUS gloves and OptiTrack.

tracking.note: Paper: IMU measurements fused with optical tracking data; MANO fitted to the keypoints by L-BFGS.
Rigid marker backplate on the Metaglove; 1.2 m x 1.8 m workspace; eSync hardware sync.
49 scanned object meshes registered in the OptiTrack frame.

unconfirmed: hours=11.8 derived from 5.1M frames (Table 1) at the 120 Hz kinematic/pose rate; the paper states no duration, and the frame count could be counted differently (e.g. per hand).
Number of distinct tasks not stated (only single-hand vs bimanual and action types in a Sankey figure).
No RGB/egocentric video is described as part of the dataset.
Tactile glove maker/model not named.
scenes=1: all capture is in one OptiTrack workspace (lab).
Project page shows Code/Data as 'Coming Soon'.

datasets.name: T-Rex
datasets.title: T-Rex: Tactile-Reactive Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Bimanual teleoperation on two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands with five fingertip tactile sensors each, in LeRobot format.
datasets.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on Dexmate Vega-1

sensor.note: Five fingertip sensors per hand, each storing a raw sensor image, a deformation map and a 6-axis wrench. No palm sensing.

scale.text: Public release: ~50 h, 5,464 episodes, 207 objects (paper: 100 h)

datasets.access: Hugging Face, ungated, 1.53 TB, LeRobot v3.
caveats: Fingertips only.

datasets.name: OpenTouch
datasets.title: OpenTouch: Bringing Full-Hand Touch to Real-World Interaction
datasets.summary: In-the-wild right-hand pressure glove with Meta Aria egocentric video, Rokoko hand pose and text labels across 14 environments.

sensor.note: FPC-routed 16 x 16 electrode grid around a commercial piezoresistive film, 169 taxels on the palmar side; normal pressure only; ESP-NOW wireless.

scale.text: 5.1 h recorded, 2,900 annotated clips (3 h), ~800 object types, 14 environments, 29 grasp types

datasets.access: Google Drive, via scripts/download_data.sh in the code repo.
caveats: Right hand only.

cameras.model: Meta Project Aria glasses (RGB POV camera, 110 deg FOV)

tracking.note: IMU + EMF sensor fusion, seven 6-DoF sensors per glove, 30 Hz; right hand only. Release HDF5 has right_hand_landmarks (21x3), right_wrist_pos, right_palm_pos.

other: Aria camera poses per frame (camera_poses in release HDF5)
GPT-5 clip labels: object, object category, environment, action, grasp type, description

sources: local: ~/data/ext/opentouch (repo README, scripts/download_data.sh, ann/final_annotations/*.csv, dl/*.hdf5) -- read only
unconfirmed: objects: paper text and project page say 'over 8,000 objects from 14 categories', but the paper's Table 1 says ~800 object types; the released annotations have 2,038 distinct object names and 110 category labels.
Number of participants not stated.
tasks left null: free exploration, no predefined task list; annotations carry 66 distinct action labels and 29 GRASP-taxonomy grasp types.

scene_types derived from release file prefixes (eat_mcdonalds, eat_ygf, fablab_ml, grocery_plant/target/tj, hardware_homedepot, home_bedroom/kitchen, office_csail/ml, sports_dicks): 12 distinct locations in the local copy vs 14 environments in the paper.
Local annotation CSVs contain 2,958 clips totalling 3.0 h (paper: 2,900 clips, 3 h).
Aria SLAM cameras and IMU were recorded (profile 28) but only RGB appears in the release HDF5.
Paper is ambiguous on finger coverage: 'uniformly cover the fingers and palmar surface'.

datasets.name: EgoTactile
datasets.title: EgoTactile: Learning Grasp Pressure for Everyday Objects from Egocentric Video
datasets.summary: Full-hand 162-sensor pressure glove with egocentric video of grasps on 63 everyday objects, plus a bare-hand test set.

sensor.note: 162-sensor glove (raw 256-channel vector), 0-350 N; resampled with sample-and-hold to a 15 Hz synchronized timeline. Layout per the code: 4x3 block per fingertip, a 6-sensor group on each finger's middle/proximal segments (averaged), and the palm.

scale.text: 5.82 h, 768 gloved-hand clips (+75 bare-hand clips, 0.61 h), 63 objects in 7 categories, 12 participants, green-screen lab

datasets.access: Hugging Face, 5.48 GB.
caveats: Grasping everyday objects rather than dexterous manipulation.
No hand pose.
Video is released at 15 fps; 692 gloved clips (11 subjects) are on Hugging Face so far, against 768 in the paper.

other: object metadata (name, category, weight, material, fill state)
participant metadata (gender, hand length; paper adds age, weight, body fat)
bare-hand subset with off-camera gloved-hand labels

sources: local: ~/data/ext/egotactile (card README, sample clip data.json + video.mp4)
unconfirmed: Camera captures at 30 fps; released clips are 15 fps (ffprobe and card). Paper uses both head and neck mounts; the card says head-mounted.

Glove maker not named. A co-author is affiliated with JQ Industries (Qingdao), and TactiDex reports a glove with the same spec (162 elements, ~17 Hz) as piezoresistive; neither establishes maker or principle here.

episodes/hours are the paper's gloved-hand totals (768 clips, 5.82 h). The bare-hand set adds 75 clips / 0.61 h. HF currently has 692 gloved clips (11 subjects, 63 objects) and 75 bare-hand clips (3 subjects, 25 objects).
frames=319k from paper Table 1.
Segmentation masks are used as model conditions in the paper but are not listed in the release card.
scenes=1: controlled green-screen lab.

datasets.name: HRDexDB
datasets.title: HRDexDB: A 4D Dexterous Grasping Dataset Across Human and Multiple Robot Embodiments
datasets.summary: Paired human and robot grasps (Allegro, two Inspire hands, Robotiq) with 21 cameras and object 6D pose; tactile on the robot fingertips only.
datasets.hand: Human (no tactile); Allegro V5 Plus, Inspire RH56DFTP, Inspire RH56F1, Robotiq 2F-85

sensor.note: Robot fingertip sensors only; the authors call them too noisy or sparse to use as contact labels.

scale.text: 3,215 trials (541 human), 100 objects, 43.5M frames

datasets.access: Hugging Face, 1.57 TB.
caveats: Grasping only.
No human tactile.

datasets.name: ActionSense
datasets.title: ActionSense: A Multimodal Dataset and Recording Framework for Human Activities Using Wearable Sensors in a Kitchen Environment
datasets.summary: Kitchen activities with bimanual tactile gloves, finger bend sensors, EMG, body IMUs, eye tracking and multi-view video.
datasets.hand: Conductive-thread tactile gloves (open finger) + Manus Prime II

sensor.note: 32 x 32 conductive-thread matrix on a pressure-sensitive film, routed to a 23x19 palm grid, 5x9 thumb, 11x4 little finger and 13x4 on each other finger; open-finger gloves, so no fingertips.

scale.text: ~13 h (778 min, 543.5 min of activities), 574 labeled activity instances, 20 activities, 10 subjects, 1 mock kitchen

datasets.access: HDF5 files at data.csail.mit.edu/ActionNet.
caveats: Subjects S06-S09 have no tactile or finger tracking.
Tactile rate is about 6 Hz in practice (the sensor table says 15 Hz).

tracking.note: 60 Hz; body segment poses and joint angles, re-processed in MVN Analyze
bend sensors + optional IMUs, 60 Hz; IMUs disabled in some experiments (no lateral finger spread); site warns finger data may be unreliable
hand segment pose from the body suit; Myo armbands also give forearm orientation

other: scale weight readings for tactile calibration

unconfirmed: hours = 778.0 min total (includes calibration routines) / 60; activity time alone is 543.5 min (~9.1 h).
episodes = 574 labeled activity instances over 9 subjects (supplement Table 1, 324.26 min labeled); the continuous recordings themselves are one or a few splits per subject.
Tactile rate: paper Table 2 lists 15 Hz, supplement HDF5 table lists a typical achieved rate of 6 Hz ('improveable to ~15').
Pupil Core world-camera resolution is not stated; 30 Hz is the world-video frame timestamp rate.

Which subjects have tactile/finger data: supplement says the last 5 of the 9 wearable-data subjects had no gloves; data page says S06-S09 (4 subjects), and S01 lost its wearable data after the first activity.
taxels_per_hand 682 = 23x19 + 5x9 + 11x4 + 3x(13x4), computed from the stated grids.

datasets.name: STAG
datasets.title: Learning the signatures of the human grasp using a scalable tactile glove
datasets.summary: Knitted glove with 548 piezoresistive sensors over the whole hand; 135K frames of single-hand grasps on 26 objects.

sensor.note: Force-sensitive film addressed by 64 orthogonal conductive-thread electrodes (32x32 readout, 548 valid elements) on a knitted glove; raw values stored as Nx32x32 int16 (500-1024).
sensor.range: working range 30 mN-0.5 N per element (responds from ~25 mN, saturates above 0.8 N)

scale.text: >5 h, 135,187 tactile frames (object set) + 11,682 (weights) + 24,037 (hand poses), 26 objects, 1 subject, right hand

datasets.access: Zip archives on stag.csail.mit.edu, with pressure-only lite versions.
caveats: Grasping and object identification rather than dexterous manipulation.
All recordings are from one person (right hand).
No hand tracking; grasp-type labels are inferred from the tactile maps.
unconfirmed: hours: paper says total recordings 'exceeding 5 hours'; 135,187 frames / 7.3 fps = 5.1 h.

episodes = 26 objects x 3 recordings (each object sequence recorded three times on different days) for the classification set; empty-hand recordings, the weight set (multiple sessions per object) and the 7 hand-pose sessions are extra and not counted.
Camera images were recorded 'for illustration' synchronized to the tactile frames (~7.3 fps); resolution and mount are not stated.
All recordings were made by one person (author S.S.) wearing the glove on the right hand.

datasets.name: Tactile textiles
datasets.title: Learning human-environment interactions using conformal tactile textiles
datasets.summary: Machine-knitted piezoresistive wearables including a full-hand glove; the glove data covers calibration and 26-object classification.

sensor.note: 722 sensors over 160 cm2; coaxial piezoresistive fibres inlaid orthogonally in a machine-knitted glove, read by a 32x32 grounding-based circuit (10-bit, Arduino Nano).
sensor.range: single sensor ~8 kOhm to 2 kOhm over 0.1-2 N; knit configurations up to 87.5 kPa

scale.text: glove: 108,305 scale-paired calibration frames + 26-object classification set; >1M tactile frames across all wearables at ~14 Hz; 1 subject

datasets.access: Dropbox links in the code repository.
caveats: Glove data is object classification, not manipulation.

tracking.note: 50 Hz, 19 joints; only for the sock pose dataset, not the glove

other: tactile socks, vest and KUKA arm sleeve recordings

unconfirmed: objects = 26 comes only from the released data folder name 'glove_objclaassification_26obj' and the train_26obj script in the code repo; the paper text does not describe the glove object set.
frames = 108,305 counts only the glove calibration pairs; the size of the glove object-classification set is not stated.
rate ~14 Hz is stated for the whole dataset (socks 13-14 Hz); no glove-specific rate given.
Xsens is described only as a worn 'MOCAP' system; 'imu' is inferred from the product.
Reporting summary: one female subject from the research group.

datasets.name: VTDexManip
datasets.title: VTDexManip: A Dataset and Benchmark for Visual-tactile Pretraining and Dexterous Manipulation with Reinforcement Learning
datasets.summary: Piezoresistive tactile gloves with egocentric HoloLens 2 video across 10 manipulation tasks and 182 objects, for visual-tactile pretraining.

sensor.note: 20 commercial thin-film pressure sensors per glove (18.3 mm on the thumb tip and palm, 10 mm elsewhere), STM32 + AD7606 readout; each pad calibrated with an F/T sensor at 0.5-7.5 N; left and right gloves exist.
sensor.range: 10 mm pads 20 g-2 kg, 18 mm pads 20 g-6 kg

scale.text: 2,032 sequences, ~565K visual-tactile frame pairs, 10 tasks, 182 objects, 5 subjects

datasets.access: OneDrive (password vtdexmanip, given in the repository).
caveats: Sparse pads rather than a dense array.
No hand pose.
unconfirmed: frames: paper states '565k' visual-tactile frame pairs (rounded).
HoloLens 2 video resolution and frame rate are not stated, so hours cannot be derived.
Sensor maker not named; the conversion module is labelled RKXS4040 and the sensors only as 'thin film pressure sensor'.
The paper mentions calibration for both left- and right-hand gloves, but does not say whether any sequences are bimanual (the per-task table lists single-hand tasks).

Per-task trajectories (Table 8) sum to 2,032: PickUp 250, BottleCap 300, In-hand Reorientation 205, Bowl Unstacking 269, Articulated 168, Peg-in-hole 153, Pouring 196, Table-top 196, Scissors 106, Pressing 189.

datasets.name: ADL-21
datasets.title: Dataset of Tactile Signatures of the Human Right Hand in Twenty-One Activities of Daily Living
datasets.summary: Tekscan Grip pressure system on the right hand of 22 subjects performing 21 activities of daily living.
datasets.hand: Tekscan Grip 4256E sewn on a glove

sensor.note: 361 sensels in 18 regions on the volar hand, 4 mm pitch (16 mm2 per sensel), on a 29x25 manufacturer matrix; sewn on a cotton glove under polyethylene and latex gloves.

scale.text: ~1.8 h, 462 trials (21 ADL x 22 subjects, one each), 18 hand-held objects, 6 lab setups

datasets.access: Zenodo, about 50 MB.
caveats: Tactile only: no video or hand pose.

other: total grip force and per-region contribution

unconfirmed: hours and frames computed from the released dataset.mat: 462 presRaw arrays totaling 324,747 rows at 50 Hz = 1.80 h (mean 14.06 s per trial, matching the paper's 'close to 14 s').
episodes = 462: the dataset is a 21x22 struct array and each subject performed each task once.
objects = 18 counts the items in the paper's Figure 2 (a-p, with (g) = spoon, knife, fork); fixtures such as the door handle, water tap and drawer are excluded.
scenes = 6 lab setups (Figure 1), all in one laboratory, so scene_types is empty.
The paper calls the sensor a 'thin resistive pressure sensor'; piezoresistive follows the Tekscan product class.

datasets.name: Reach&Grasp
datasets.title: Reach&Grasp: a multimodal dataset of the whole upper-limb during simple and complex movements
datasets.summary: Upper-limb reaching and grasping with a tactile glove, CyberGlove joint angles, Vicon motion capture and high-density EMG.

sensor.note: 17 palm taxels in three groups plus 41 on the fingers (index/pinky 9, middle/ring 8, thumb 7); uncalibrated; taxels 9, 11 and 14 (ring fingertip) are faulty.
sensor.range: uncalibrated (raw ADC, no N or Pa conversion)

scale.text: ~2.8 h of tactile, 158 recordings (10 subjects x 16 tasks, 10 repetitions each), 4 objects

datasets.access: IIT Dataverse (DOI 10.48557/L6OWMM), BIDS format.
caveats: Reach-and-grasp movements rather than dexterous manipulation.
No video.

tracking.system: Vicon (10 IR cameras, 23 markers, RHand Bodybuilder model)
tracking.note: 100 Hz finger MCP/thumb joint angles
100 Hz MCP/PIP, thumb, abduction, wrist pitch/yaw; per-subject scaling
wrist, elbow and shoulder joint angles, 100 Hz

other: bipolar EMG 10 ch (Cometa Wave Plus, 2 kHz)

unconfirmed: hours = sum of RecordingDuration in the 158 released tactile JSON sidecars (9,949 s); the paper only says each session lasted ~1 h including rests.
episodes = 158 tactile recordings (one per subject-task; FroRea and ReaCyl have 9 subjects each); each recording holds 10 repetitions, so ~1,580 repetitions.
objects = 4 (glass, bottle cap, table tennis ball, tennis ball), from paper Fig. 3B.
Sessions were video-recorded but the video is not released (available on request).

datasets.name: HATO
datasets.title: Learning Visuotactile Skills with Two Multifingered Hands
datasets.summary: Bimanual teleoperation of two Psyonic Ability hands on UR5e arms, with fingertip pressure sensing and three RGB-D cameras.

sensor.note: Six pressure sensors per fingertip.

scale.text: 800 demonstrations, 4 tasks

datasets.access: Berkeley Box, with a download script in the repository.
caveats: Fingertips only.

datasets.name: T-Dex
datasets.title: Dexterity from Touch: Self-Supervised Pre-Training of Tactile Representations with Robotic Play
datasets.summary: Allegro hand covered with XELA uSkin pads, recorded during 2.5 hours of teleoperated play plus task demonstrations.

sensor.note: 15 XELA uSkin pads (4 per finger, 3 on the thumb), each 4 x 4 three-axis taxels.

scale.text: ~2.5 h play data plus 6 demonstrations per task, 5 tasks

datasets.access: Google Drive, linked from the project page.
caveats: No palm sensing reported.

datasets.name: Humanoid VTA
datasets.title: A Humanoid Visual-Tactile-Action Dataset for Contact-Rich Manipulation
datasets.summary: Humanoid with two Inspire hands carrying 1,062 tactile sensors each over fingers and palm, teleoperated on deformable-object tasks.
datasets.hand: Inspire RH56DFX x 2 on a humanoid

sensor.note: Sensor technology not stated. A tactile carpet under the robot is recorded too.

scale.text: 101.9K frames, 4 tasks, ~80 episodes per task

datasets.access: No release link found as of 2026-10-15.

datasets.name: TACROSS
datasets.title: TACROSS: An Efficient and Low-Cost Scalable Human Touch System Across Heterogeneous Tactile Sensors
datasets.summary: Piezoresistive fabric glove for large-scale human touch collection, paired with robot data from a capacitive Revo2 tactile hand.
datasets.hand: Fabric tactile glove; BrainCo Revo2 tactile hand

sensor.note: Human glove: 12x15 palm array + five 3x7 finger arrays = 285 physical locations, 256 values streamed per frame (12-bit ADC, serial/BLE), ~200 cm2, >85% coverage. Robot side: BrainCo Revo2 tactile hand (capacitive), sampled at 30 Hz.
sensor.model: TACROSS glove (5-layer Cu-Ni fabric electrodes + pressure-sensitive layer); robot: Revo2 tactile hand
sensor.range: 0-20 N per taxel (force test, max 83.91/255 ADC, no saturation); repeatability 1.38% F.S., hysteresis 11.65% F.S.

scale.text: 183.95 h (159.09 h human + 24.86 h robot); 24,913 recorded / 22,486 valid episodes (human 23,677 / 21,412; robot 1,236 / 1,074); 4 robot evaluation tasks

datasets.access: Release planned by the authors.

cameras.note: human capture; labelled 'RGB (front)' / 'egocentric RGB'; mount position not stated
robot side; 'three 240x320 RGB views' fed to ACT at 15 Hz; native recording resolution and placement not stated

tracking.system: HaMeR (Vision-IK Ego config, 21 3-D keypoints from RGB, 30 Hz)
tracking.note: human, Ego-V configuration (69.60 h, 10,893 demos)
human, Ego-R configuration (89.49 h, 12,784 demos); hand pose 30 Hz

tracking.system: 7-DoF arm (model not named) + BrainCo Revo2 (6 active DoF)
tracking.note: robot side; actions 8-D (arm + open/close) or 13-D (arm + 6 hand)

unconfirmed: episodes = 24,913 recorded (human+robot); valid = 22,486. Current entry's 21,412 is valid HUMAN demos only.
Paper says 'release 183.95 h of recorded trajectories'; whether invalid episodes are included in the release is not stated.

tasks: corpus task count not stated; only 4 closed-loop evaluation tasks (dispensing, liquid transfer, pipetting, fruit pick-and-place) are described. Scene types from project page ('industrial, home, laboratory and outdoor settings').
Fig. 3 caption says '256 channels (180 palm + 105 finger sensors)' which sums to 285; 285 physical locations vs 256 streamed values per the text.
Human camera is a RealSense D435i but only RGB is described; depth not mentioned.
Coverage 'fingers' = five 3x7 finger arrays; exact phalanx extent not stated in text.
Robot camera models and mounts not given (Fig. 6 shows 'RGB cameras').
Rokoko glove model / sensing principle not named in paper, so method left null.

datasets.name: DexViTac
datasets.title: DexViTac: Collecting Human Visuo-Tactile-Kinematic Demonstrations for Contact-Rich Dexterous Manipulation
datasets.summary: Human demonstrations with fingertip tactile arrays, Manus finger tracking and a hand-mounted fisheye camera, matched by identical sensors on an Inspire hand.
datasets.hand: Glove with fingertip arrays + Manus Metagloves; Inspire RH56DFTP

sensor.note: Five HIT LongLin-96 fingertip modules, each 8x16 taxels over ~140 mm2, in finger sleeves on a Manus glove; identical modules on the Inspire RH56DFTP robot hand. Sampled at 1000 Hz but the stored, synchronized stream uses tactile at 60 Hz as the anchor timeline.

scale.text: 2,400+ human demonstrations, 40+ tasks in 4 task categories, 10+ real-world environments

datasets.access: Hugging Face repository exists but is empty ("near future").
caveats: Fingertips only.

cameras.model: GoPro Hero 12 Black + Max Lens Mod 2.0
cameras.note: human side; 177 deg FOV; paper calls it 'first-person' but Fig. 2 shows it mounted on the back of the hand/wrist next to the glove
robot side; mounted below the robot wrist on a multi-DOF bracket, optical centre aligned to middle fingertip within +/-12 deg

tracking.note: human; 19-DOF stretch/spread parameters at 120 Hz (downsampled to 60 Hz); paper describes the gloves as IMU-equipped
human; 6-DoF pose at 200 Hz, nearest-neighbour matched to 60 Hz; T265 mounted on the hand dorsum
robot evaluation platform; human data retargeted via PyBullet IK

unconfirmed: Counts are lower bounds ('2,400+', '40+', '10+'). Scene types are the examples listed ('including kitchens, homes, retail spaces, and offices').
Hours not stated; mean 14.5 s/demo is given only for the 4 evaluation tasks, so no total derived.
Tactile principle not stated (only 'flexible pressure-sensitive sensors'); maker of LongLin-96 not identified beyond the 'HIT' prefix.
Manus Quantum classified 'magnetic' per catalog schema; the paper itself says the gloves are 'equipped with IMUs'.
Camera role: paper says first-person, but the hardware figure shows it hand/wrist-mounted; recorded as wrist.
Whether robot-side recordings are part of the released dataset is not stated; the dataset is described as human demonstrations.
wrist_cameras = 1 for each side (human and robot).

datasets.name: OSMO
datasets.title: OSMO: Open-Source Tactile Glove for Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer
datasets.summary: Open-source glove with three-axis magnetic taxels on fingertips and palm; human wiping demonstrations, with the same glove worn by the robot hand at deployment.

sensor.note: 12 three-axis taxels (5 fingertips + palm in three sections); each sensor PCB has two Bosch BMM350 3-axis magnetometers (differential, MuMetal-shielded) and a BHI360 6-axis IMU; raw flux in uT is used as tactile data. Paper policy and the public sample use only the 5 fingertips (30 values = 5 x 2 mags x 3 axes). Streams logged at 25 Hz.
sensor.maker: custom (Meta FAIR); DIY kit sold by WowRobo

scale.text: ~2 h, 140 human wiping demonstrations in the robot workspace; no robot demonstrations

datasets.access: One sample demonstration on Google Drive, linked from the repository's data/README.md (2025-12-21); the full 140-demo set is not released yet. Hardware, firmware and code are open.
caveats: Hand pose is estimated from video (HaMeR, refined with stereo IR depth).
One task (wiping); the released sample uses the fingertip taxels only.
No robot data is recorded; the robot is used only for deployment.

cameras.note: human capture; single scene camera, extrinsically calibrated to the robot base; same placement used at robot deployment
left/right IR images, cropped to ROI with white fill in the public sample; used offline for FoundationStereo depth

tracking.note: human; 3-D keypoints and hand mesh from RGB
